scenario.title: Battle of Athens
intro.text:
BATTLE OF ATHENS - 12 DEC 1944

Athens, Greece

After the withdrawal of the Germans from Greece, the royalists have returned to our country and think they can - with the help of the disgusting Brits - rob the fruits of our liberation struggle! They also not shy away from massacre peaceful protesters to keep themselves in power. Once again it's time to take up arms and to chase these parasites out of our country!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE The British will try to fly in reinforcements, so occupy as soon as possible all airfields!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-23-0-briliant.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
line.reaction-23-0-briliant.text: The road force was trapped and the key positions fell before relief arrived. ELAS has gained weapons, prisoners, and responsibility for the settlements now exposed by its victory.
line.reaction-23-1-victory-tactical.text: The objectives were taken, though part of the column escaped and some villages remained within range of the withdrawing guns. Liberation is approaching with armed Greek organisations already measuring one another.
line.callback-0.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
line.callback-0.text: The Agorelitsa guns now belong to ELAS. They frighten the occupier and reassure every Greek who suspected we were preparing for a larger fight. The same barrel can do both.
line.callback-1.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
line.callback-1.text: The reprisal columns found empty villages behind the Agorelitsa roadblocks. We captured fewer guns. The families who returned have not complained about the exchange.
line.edes-disarmament-memory.speaker: Aris Velouchiotis
line.edes-disarmament-memory.text: You took the rifles from EDES before Britain could make more use of them. Britain has brought its own troops now. There is no pass narrow enough for this argument.
line.edes-amnesty-memory.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.edes-amnesty-memory.text: Some men who left Kalabaka under our terms are inside these districts with their families. They know we once allowed an enemy to walk away. That memory may open a door no order can.
line.scene-0.speaker: Georgios Siantos
line.scene-0.text: Scobie demands that ELAS disarm while the government keeps the formations brought from abroad. Accept that and legal politics begins at the pleasure of British guns.
line.scene-1.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-1.text: This is Major Hale on the line. The airfields and Piraeus will be opened. British reinforcements are not a bluff, and I will not insult you by presenting them as one.
line.scene-2.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-2.text: I know your voice, Edward. I also know how quickly your lorries and guns can turn a bridgehead into a front. Do you know who lives between your phase lines?
line.scene-3.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
line.scene-3.text: A rush for the airfields might delay that weight. It will also put our best battalions where naval guns and aircraft can reach them together.
line.scene-4.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-4.text: The western districts are already cutting windows into basement walls so families can pass without crossing the streets. Whatever plan we choose will arrive after the civilians have understood the battle.
line.decision.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
line.decision.text: Do we strike the airfields, Piraeus, and the centre before the bridgehead hardens, or hold coherent districts and leave a channel for settlement?
line.decision.choice.seize-the-entry-poi: Strike the airfields, Piraeus, and central approaches before British reinforcements deploy.
Spend 75 prestige, give infantry and anti-aircraft formations 20 experience, and fully rearm the core.
Build a coherent district defence and keep channels for a settlement open.
Restore the core to full strength with full fuel and ammunition and give infantry 10 experience.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-a-0.text: Then we meet as enemies. I am sorry for that, Commander. It changes none of my fire orders.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Georgios Siantos
line.choice-a-1.text: Every available battalion moves before the British line settles. We are not asking permission to remain part of Greek political life.
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
line.choice-a-2.text: I will issue the order. Keep one reserve out of the race for landmarks, or there will be no army left to exploit success.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Georgios Siantos
line.choice-b-0.text: A defensive posture lets Papandreou call this a police action while British strength accumulates. If talks fail, the lost hours are yours.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Stefanos Sarafis
line.choice-b-1.text: They are. District sectors, local reserves, open liaison between them. We hold enough of Athens to negotiate without gambling the army on runways.
line.choice-b-2.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-b-2.text: I will send the corridor markings to both sides. Hale may ignore them. The hospitals will still know we tried before the shells arrived.
